newsitem.title: INDIA: India depository transaction costs sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: India depository transaction costs sharply lower.

text.p: Transaction costs of depository shares will be sharply lower than the cost of purchasing or selling physical shares, the managing director of India's National Securities Depository Ltd (NSDL) said on Thursday.
The NSDL, India's first share depository which will introduce paperless trading on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), is due to be launched on Friday.
NSDL Managing Director C.B. Bhave said there was "virtually no comparison" between the transaction costs involved in shares which will be part of the depository and physical shares.

"For insitutional investors the cost of transacting physical shares will be say, for a buyer, 50 basis points for stamp duty, about 30 basis points for handling the transaction and a custody charge of 30-35 basis points," Bhave said.
He said the depository had set a transaction charge of five basis points and a custody charge of seven basis points.
"The transaction cost drops dramatically," Bhave said.
Bhave said initially the depository would adhere to the weekly settlement cycle on the NSE.
"The advantage will be that one day after the pay-out day the purchaser would actually receive credit in his account. He is the owner and can sell the shares the next day," Bhave said.
Currently transfer procedures for physical shares take more than three months in India.
